root_cause.text: The `mvpp2_rx` function in the Marvell PPv2 network driver performs a DMA sync starting at the base DMA address (`dma_addr`) instead of accounting for the hardware packet offset (`MVPP2_SKB_HEADROOM`), which can lead to the CPU reading stale cache contents at the end of the received frame on non-coherent DMA systems.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff replaces `dma_sync_single_for_cpu` with `dma_sync_single_range_for_cpu` in `mvpp2_rx` to apply an offset of `MVPP2_SKB_HEADROOM` to the DMA sync range, ensuring the sync covers the actual received packet data rather than the unused headroom.

Because the sync starts at `dma_addr` and only covers `rx_bytes + MVPP2_MH_SIZE` bytes, the end of the received frame (which is shifted by the headroom offset) is not synced, leading to stale cache reads on non-coherent systems.
